- **[Quick start](https://straitlink.in/docs/quick-start/)**: create a workspace, add your app, make a link and test it on a real phone. The dashboard part takes about 10 minutes, the SDK installs from GitHub, and testing deferred links on Android needs a Google Play internal testing build.
- **[Migrate from Firebase Dynamic Links](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-firebase/)**: bring your old `page.link` links across.
- **[Migrate from Branch](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-branch/)**: import your Branch link export with deep link paths, fallbacks and previews, and plan the cutover.
- **[Troubleshooting](https://straitlink.in/docs/troubleshooting/)**: the link opened the browser instead of the app? Start here.

| Platform | Package | Guide |
|---|---|---|
| React Native and Expo | `@strait/sdk-react-native` | [React Native and Expo](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/) |
| Flutter | `strait_sdk` | [Flutter](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/flutter/) |
| Android (Kotlin) | `strait-sdk-android` | [Android](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/android/) |
| iOS (Swift) | `StraitSDK` (Swift Package Manager) | [iOS](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/ios/) |
| Unity (C#) | `strait-sdk-unity` | [Unity](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/unity/) |
| Web | `@strait/sdk-web` | [Web](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/web/) |
| Node (your server) | `@strait/sdk-node` | [Node](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/node/) |

The React Native, iOS (Swift), Flutter and Unity SDKs are at version 0.8.0, the Android SDK at 0.7.2, the Node SDK at 0.6.2 and the web SDK at 0.5.2. The app SDKs follow one shared contract: the same link events, the same app-state labels, the same offline retry for analytics. Each SDK's core is checked against the same shared test files, so a link behaves the same in every one. The Unity guide's engine glue (MonoBehaviour, PlayerPrefs, the iOS plugin) hasn't been run in the Unity editor yet; see [Unity](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/unity/).

1. **Your workspace** has a link domain, `<your-handle>.strait.link`, and two keys.
2. **A link** like `https://acme.strait.link/summer` points at a destination such as `https://shop.example.com/product/42`.
3. **When someone taps it**, the phone opens your app directly (verified App Links / Universal Links), or our server sends them to the store or your website.
4. **The SDK in your app** turns the link into a path and parameters you route to, including on the first open after an install, and reports the open for analytics.
5. **Your server** creates links and sends purchase events with the secret key, and can receive webhooks.

| Key | Looks like | Where it goes | What it can do |
|---|---|---|---|
| Publishable key | `st_pub_live_…` | Your app and website | Resolve links, report opens, match installs, send events |
| Secret key | `st_live_…` | Your server only | Create, list, update and deactivate links, send events |

The publishable key is in **Dashboard → Get started**. Secret keys are in **Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys**. Never put a secret key in an app or a web page.

**Publishable key.** Rotate it in **Dashboard → Get started**. You get a new key straight away, and the old one keeps working for **7 days**, so apps already on people's phones keep working while you ship an update with the new key. During those 7 days, responses to the old key carry a `Strait-Key-Deprecated` header with the time it stops working (ISO 8601, for example `2026-01-08T12:00:00.000Z`). After that, the old key gets `401`. If you rotate again within the 7 days, the key from the earlier rotation stops at once: only one old key is honoured.

**Secret keys.** You can have several. Each one in **Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys** shows when it was last used ("never used" if it hasn't been), so you can spot a key nothing uses any more before you revoke it. We store only a hash, so a new key is shown once. Revoking a secret key stops it immediately. To replace one without downtime, create the new key, deploy it, check the old key's last-used date has stopped moving, then revoke the old one.

Android and web are live. iPhone support (Universal Links and deferred deep links) is built and covered by automated tests, but hasn't yet been proven on a real iPhone, so it's in **beta**. Live service health is on the [status page](https://status.strait.link).

| Part | What it needs |
|---|---|
| Dashboard: workspace, app details, keys, first link (steps 1 to 4) | About 10 minutes |
| SDK in your app (steps 5 and 6) | About 15 minutes. Install it straight from GitHub; no sign-up or access request |
| Testing deferred links on Android (step 7, test 2) | A build installed from Google Play internal testing. The first upload and review can take 1 to 2 hours |

Deep links to an installed app can be tested with a local build as soon as steps 1 to 6 are done.

[Sign up](https://app.straitlink.in/?signup=1). Your workspace gets its own link domain:

```txt
https://<your-handle>.strait.link
```

:::warn Pick your handle before you create a link
Your handle comes from your workspace name. To change it, go to **Dashboard → Get started** (or **Settings**) before you create any link. After your first link the handle is fixed, because shared links and your app's link setup depend on it. Only the workspace owner can change it.
:::

In these docs we use `acme.strait.link`; your own handle is shown in the dashboard. Each workspace has its own subdomain because phones verify **one app per domain**: your subdomain serves your app's verification files, so your links open your app. See [Link domains](https://straitlink.in/docs/link-domains/).

In **Dashboard → Settings**, fill in what you have:

| Platform | Fields | Where to find them |
|---|---|---|
| Android | Package name, custom scheme, SHA-256 certificate fingerprints | `applicationId` in `build.gradle` (Expo: `android.package` in `app.json`); your scheme (for example `yourapp`); see below for SHA-256 |
| iPhone | Apple Team ID, bundle ID, App Store ID | Apple Developer → Membership; Xcode target (Expo: `ios.bundleIdentifier`); App Store Connect |
| Everyone else | Default web URL (`https://` only) | Where desktop visitors and people without the app should go |
| Branding (optional) | App name, icon URL, brand colour | Shown on the pages people see when a tap can't open your app straight away. See [App Links](https://straitlink.in/docs/app-links/#how-your-link-pages-look) |

Also choose **when someone without the app taps a link** on Android: Google Play if the app is published, always Google Play (use this while testing with Play internal testers), or always your website.

:::warn Add every SHA-256 you sign with
Android checks the certificate of the build that's installed. Add your **debug** key for local builds, your **upload** key for sideloaded release builds, and the **Play App Signing** key for anything installed from Google Play (Play Console → Test and release → App integrity). Missing the Play key is the most common reason links open the browser instead of the app.

Paste fingerprints in any form: upper or lower case, with or without colons. We save them as uppercase with colons and drop duplicates. Anything that isn't a SHA-256 fingerprint (64 hex characters) is refused with a message saying which entry is wrong.
:::

Find your fingerprints:

```bash
# Native Android project (Android Studio's shared debug key)
keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore -alias androiddebugkey -storepass android -keypass android | grep SHA256

# React Native, or Expo after `npx expo prebuild`: the project's own debug key
keytool -list -v -keystore android/app/debug.keystore -storepass android | grep SHA256

# EAS Build: choose Android and your build profile; the keystore's SHA-256 is listed
eas credentials
```

:::note Testing deferred links on Android
A link tapped before the app is installed reaches the app through Google Play's install referrer, so test 2 in [step 7](#7-test-on-a-real-phone) needs a build installed from Google Play. Upload a build to **internal testing** in Play Console, add yourself as a tester, add the Play App Signing SHA-256 above, and choose **Always Google Play** for "when someone without the app taps a link" while you test. The first upload and review can take 1 to 2 hours.
:::

- **Publishable key** (`st_pub_live_…`): in **Dashboard → Get started**. Goes in your app. Safe to ship.
- **Secret key** (`st_live_…`): create one in **Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys** (Get started links there). It's shown once. Server only: keep it in an environment variable.

In **Dashboard → Links**, or from your server:

```bash
export SECRET_KEY=st_live_…   # Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys
curl https://strait.link/v1/links \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "slug": "summer", "longUrl": "https://shop.example.com/product/42" }'
```

Your link is now `https://acme.strait.link/summer`. The destination must be `https://`; your app receives its path (`/product/42`) and query parameters.

:::note No website?
The destination can be any `https://` URL on a domain you control, or your default web URL from step 2 with the path you want, such as `https://yourapp.com/product/42`. Only the path and query reach your app. Desktop visitors go to the full URL, and so do people without the app if you chose "always your website", so it's best if that page exists.
:::

sections.section: 5. Let the phone open your app
sections.markdown:
**Android**: add an App Links intent filter for your link domain, plus your custom scheme (used when a browser hands the link to your app):

```xml title="AndroidManifest.xml"
<activity android:name=".MainActivity" android:launchMode="singleTask" android:exported="true">
  
  <intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
    <data android:scheme="https" android:host="acme.strait.link" />
  </intent-filter>
  
  <intent-filter>
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
    <data android:scheme="yourapp" />
  </intent-filter>
</activity>
```

**iPhone (beta)**: in Xcode, add the **Associated Domains** capability with `applinks:acme.strait.link`, and register your custom URL scheme under URL Types.

**Expo**: put the same settings in `app.json`. Expo writes them into the native projects when it builds. Replace `acme.strait.link` with your own link domain:

```json title="app.json"
{
  "expo": {
    "scheme": "yourapp",
    "android": {
      "package": "com.yourcompany.yourapp",
      "intentFilters": [
        {
          "action": "VIEW",
          "autoVerify": true,
          "data": [{ "scheme": "https", "host": "acme.strait.link" }],
          "category": ["BROWSABLE", "DEFAULT"]
        }
      ]
    },
    "ios": {
      "bundleIdentifier": "com.yourcompany.yourapp",
      "associatedDomains": ["applinks:acme.strait.link"]
    }
  }
}
```

We host the verification files (`/.well-known/assetlinks.json` and `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association`) on your link domain from the details in step 2. See [App Links & Universal Links](https://straitlink.in/docs/app-links/).

Test from a **chat or email app** (Messages, WhatsApp, Gmail), not by typing the link into the address bar: phones only open apps from links that are tapped.

1. **App installed**: tap the link. The app should open on `/product/42`.
2. **App not installed**: uninstall, tap the link, install from the store, open the app. It should land on `/product/42` on first open. On Android this needs a build installed from Google Play internal testing, with **Always Google Play** chosen in Settings while you test, because the link travels through the Play install referrer. Setting that up the first time takes 1 to 2 hours (see [step 2](#2-tell-us-about-your-app)).
3. **Check Analytics** in the dashboard: you should see the tap, the app open and (for test 2) a matched install.

Link opened the browser? See [Troubleshooting](https://straitlink.in/docs/troubleshooting/).

| Platform | Package | What it covers | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|
| React Native and Expo | `@strait/sdk-react-native` | Links, deferred links (Play Install Referrer on Android), open reporting. Expo needs a development build | [React Native and Expo](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/react-native/) |
| Flutter | `strait_sdk` | The same, in pure Dart | [Flutter](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/flutter/) |
| Android (Kotlin) | `strait-sdk-android` | Native Android apps | [Android](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/android/) |
| iOS (Swift) | `StraitSDK` | Native iOS apps (beta) | [iOS](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/ios/) |
| Unity (C#) | `strait-sdk-unity` | Games on Android and iOS | [Unity](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/unity/) |

| Platform | Package | What it covers | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web | `@strait/sdk-web` | Deferred link matching for web apps and PWAs | [Web](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/web/) |
| Node | `@strait/sdk-node` | Create and manage links, send events from your backend | [Node](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/node/) |

The React Native, iOS (Swift), Flutter and Unity SDKs are at version 0.8.0, the Android SDK at 0.7.2, the Node SDK at 0.6.2 and the web SDK at 0.5.2. Each one's core is checked against the same shared test files: the same link events, app-state labels and offline retry. Two limits today:

- **iOS** is in beta: covered by automated tests, not yet proven on a real iPhone.
- **Unity**: the C# library is tested, but the Unity glue in the guide (MonoBehaviour, PlayerPrefs, the iOS plugin) hasn't been run in the Unity editor or on a device yet.

Every SDK installs from its public GitHub repo today; each guide has the exact command. npm, pub.dev, Maven Central and OpenUPM listings are coming soon.

Not using an SDK? Everything they do is in the [REST API](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/).

The SDK isn't on the npm registry yet, so install it from GitHub (npm builds it during install), together with the two packages it needs:

```bash
npm install github:bazingga08/strait-sdk-react-native#v0.8.0 @react-native-async-storage/async-storage react-native-play-install-referrer
```

It installs as `@strait/sdk-react-native`, so imports stay the same once it's on npm. In an Expo project, install the two helper packages with `npx expo install` so Expo picks versions that match your SDK.

`AsyncStorage` keeps the once-per-install flag and any open reports that couldn't be sent yet. The Play Install Referrer module gives Android installs an exact match.

Everything on this page works in Expo, with two differences.

**You need a development build, not Expo Go.** The setup uses a native module (`react-native-play-install-referrer`) and your app's own link settings. Expo Go can't load that module, and links on your domain open your app, not Expo Go. Build your app with:

```bash
npx expo run:android     # or npx expo run:ios; runs prebuild for you
eas build --profile development --platform android   # or build in the cloud with EAS Build
```

**Link settings go in `app.json`.** Replace `acme.strait.link` with your own link domain, and `yourapp` with your custom scheme (the one in Dashboard → Settings):

```json title="app.json"
{
  "expo": {
    "scheme": "yourapp",
    "android": {
      "package": "com.yourcompany.yourapp",
      "intentFilters": [
        {
          "action": "VIEW",
          "autoVerify": true,
          "data": [{ "scheme": "https", "host": "acme.strait.link" }],
          "category": ["BROWSABLE", "DEFAULT"]
        }
      ]
    },
    "ios": {
      "bundleIdentifier": "com.yourcompany.yourapp",
      "associatedDomains": ["applinks:acme.strait.link"]
    }
  }
}
```

`scheme` registers `yourapp://` on both platforms (used when a browser hands a link to your app). The intent filter with `autoVerify` makes Android open `https://acme.strait.link/…` links in your app directly, and `associatedDomains` does the same on iPhone.

**SHA-256 fingerprints for Dashboard → Settings:**

```bash
# Local builds (npx expo run:android): the project's debug key
keytool -list -v -keystore android/app/debug.keystore -storepass android | grep SHA256

# EAS builds: choose Android and your build profile; the keystore's SHA-256 is listed
eas credentials
```

For builds installed from Google Play, also add the **Play App Signing** key from Play Console → Test and release → App integrity.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `direct` (a link opened the app) or `deferred` (tapped before install) |
| `route` | `app_link`, `custom_scheme`, `install_referrer` or `fingerprint` |
| `appState` | `closed` (the link launched the app), `background` or `foreground` |
| `matched`, `reason` | When `matched` is false: `not_found`, `expired`, `password_protected`, `no_match`, `network` or `invalid_url` |
| `url`, `path`, `params` | The destination to route to |
| `linkId`, `id`, `ms`, `at` | Link id, open id, resolve time in ms, arrival time (epoch ms) |

Every time a link opens the app, the SDK reports it once. You don't write any analytics code for this.

| How the app opened | Joined to |
|---|---|
| Verified link tapped in WhatsApp, Gmail, Messages… | The link (also counted as a tap) |
| Browser handed off to the app (`yourapp://…`) | The exact tap |
| First open after a Play install | The exact tap that sent the user to the store |
| First open after an App Store install | The matched tap |
| Your own https links | Host and path only, never the query |

Reports that can't be sent (offline, server busy) are saved and retried on the next start and whenever the app comes back to the foreground, for up to 7 days (100 at most). Each open has an id, so nothing is counted twice. Navigation never waits for a report.

```ts
import { links } from './links';

links.trackEvent('purchase', { value: 49.99, currency: 'USD' }); // the tap is attached automatically
```

Events show up at the bottom of your funnel in Analytics, with revenue. `trackEvent` returns a promise that resolves to `true` when the event was accepted.

The event carries the tap id of the most recent link open, as long as that open was in the last 7 days. The tap id comes from a browser hand-off to `yourapp://…?strait_click=…`, a Google Play install, an open from a verified short link, or an iPhone install match. When our server matches an open or an install, it sends the tap id back with its answer. That lets Analytics put the revenue on the exact tap's channel and A/B variant. Each newer open replaces the remembered tap with its own, so an older tap never takes credit for a newer open; if an open comes with no tap id, the remembered one is forgotten and the event carries none. To name the tap yourself, pass `clickId`, which overrides the remembered one. The server keeps it only if it's a tap of your workspace; otherwise it drops the id and still records the event.

| Platform | Method | Precision |
|---|---|---|
| Android | Play Install Referrer | Exact |
| iPhone (beta) | Short-lived device match | Probabilistic |

See [Deferred deep linking](https://straitlink.in/docs/deferred-deep-linking/) for exactly what's collected and how long it's kept.

The SDK isn't on pub.dev yet, so add it as a git dependency in `pubspec.yaml`:

```yaml title="pubspec.yaml"
dependencies:
  strait_sdk:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/bazingga08/strait-sdk-flutter
      ref: v0.8.0
```

Then add the helper packages:

```bash
flutter pub add app_links shared_preferences play_install_referrer flutter_timezone
```

[`app_links`](https://pub.dev/packages/app_links) delivers links, [`shared_preferences`](https://pub.dev/packages/shared_preferences) stores the once-per-install flag and unsent reports, [`play_install_referrer`](https://pub.dev/packages/play_install_referrer) gives Android installs an exact match, and [`flutter_timezone`](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_timezone) provides the IANA time zone the iPhone match needs.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `direct` (a link opened the app) or `deferred` (tapped before install) |
| `route` | `app_link`, `custom_scheme`, `install_referrer`, `fingerprint` (`route.value`) |
| `appState` | `closed`, `background`, `foreground` |
| `matched`, `reason` | `not_found`, `expired`, `password_protected`, `no_match`, `network`, `invalid_url` |
| `rawUrl` | The URL the OS handed the app |
| `url`, `path`, `params` | The destination to navigate to |
| `linkId`, `ms`, `at`, `id` | Link id, resolve time, arrival time, id shared with the start signal |

Every link open is reported once, automatically, including offline opens (saved and retried for up to 7 days). To record purchases:

```dart
links.trackEvent('purchase', value: 49.99, currency: 'USD', linkId: e.linkId);
```

The event carries the tap id of the most recent link open, as long as that open was in the last 7 days. The tap id comes from a browser hand-off to `yourapp://…?strait_click=…`, a Google Play install, an open from a verified short link, or an iPhone install match. When our server matches an open or an install, it sends the tap id back with its answer. That lets Analytics put the revenue on the exact tap's channel and A/B variant. Each newer open replaces the remembered tap with its own, so an older tap never takes credit for a newer open; if an open comes with no tap id, the remembered one is forgotten and the event carries none. To name the tap yourself, pass `clickId:`, which overrides the remembered one. The server keeps it only if it's a tap of your workspace; otherwise it drops the id and still records the event.

Debugging helpers: `await links.pendingOpenReports()` (count waiting) and `await links.flushOpenReports()` (send now). `links.checkDeferred()` re-runs the deferred check without recording an install.

```dart
final result = await resolveDeferredLink(
  publishableKey: 'st_pub_live_…',
  endpoint: 'https://acme.strait.link',
  platform: Platform.isIOS ? 'ios' : 'android',
  device: device,            // DeviceFields as above
  installReferrer: referrer, // Android only; null otherwise
);
if (result.matched && result.longUrl != null) { /* route */ }
```

It never throws; on any error it returns `MatchResult.none`.

The Android SDK (strait-sdk-android 0.7.2) is served by JitPack, built from its public GitHub repo. Add the JitPack repository, then the SDK, Google's Install Referrer library and, if you don't have it, `androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-process`.

```kotlin title="settings.gradle.kts"
dependencyResolutionManagement {
    repositories {
        google()
        mavenCentral()
        maven("https://jitpack.io")
    }
}
```

```kotlin title="app/build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("com.github.bazingga08:strait-sdk-android:v0.7.2") // Strait SDK
    implementation("com.android.installreferrer:installreferrer:2.2")
    implementation("androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-process:2.8.7")
}
```

**Requirements.** The SDK is plain Kotlin, compiled with Kotlin 1.9.24 to Java 17 bytecode, so build your app with JDK 17 or newer (Android Gradle Plugin 8 already needs it). At runtime it uses the Kotlin standard library and `org.json`, which ships with Android. Everything is in the `dev.strait.sdk` package.

:::note
Network calls block the calling thread. Pass a background `executor` so `start` and `handleUrl` never run on the main thread. Listeners are called on that executor, so post to the main thread before you navigate.
:::

```kotlin
links.trackEvent("purchase", value = 49.99, currency = "USD", linkId = lastLinkId)
links.checkDeferred()   // re-run the deferred check (debugging; never records an install)
```

The event carries the tap id of the most recent link open, as long as that open was in the last 7 days. The tap id comes from a browser hand-off to `yourapp://…?strait_click=…`, a Google Play install, or an open from a verified short link. When our server matches an open or an install, it sends the tap id back with its answer. That lets Analytics put the revenue on the exact tap's channel and A/B variant. Each newer open replaces the remembered tap with its own, so an older tap never takes credit for a newer open; if an open comes with no tap id, the remembered one is forgotten and the event carries none. To name the tap yourself, pass `clickId =`, which overrides the remembered one. The server keeps it only if it's a tap of your workspace; otherwise it drops the id and still records the event.

`LinkEvent` fields: `id, kind (direct|deferred), route (app_link|custom_scheme|install_referrer|fingerprint), appState (closed|background|foreground), matched, reason, rawUrl, url, path, params, linkId, ms, at`. `onLink` replays past events to late subscribers; both `onLink` and `onLinkStart` return an unsubscribe function.

Every link open is reported once, joined to its tap where possible: verified links from chat apps, browser hand-offs, the first open after a Play install, and your own https links (host and path only). Reports that can't be sent are saved under `storage` and retried on the next `start`, whenever `onAppState(ACTIVE)` is called, and after any report that gets through, for up to 7 days (100 at most).

HTTP uses `HttpURLConnection` by default. To use OkHttp, implement `HttpTransport`: throw on network failure and return every HTTP status as an `HttpResponse`.

:::warn Beta
The iOS SDK is tested in CI against the same shared test files as every other SDK, but deferred deep linking hasn't yet been proven on a real iPhone. Use it, tell us what you see, and keep a fallback in mind for launch-critical flows.
:::

In Xcode: **File → Add Package Dependencies…**, paste `https://github.com/bazingga08/strait-sdk-swift` and pick version 0.8.0 or later. Or in `Package.swift`:

```swift title="Package.swift"
.package(url: "https://github.com/bazingga08/strait-sdk-swift", from: "0.8.0")
// target dependency: .product(name: "StraitSDK", package: "strait-sdk-swift")
```

Then in Xcode: **Signing & Capabilities → Associated Domains → `applinks:acme.strait.link`**, and add your custom scheme under **Info → URL Types**. Make sure your Apple Team ID and bundle ID are saved in Dashboard → Settings, so your link domain serves a matching `apple-app-site-association` file.

```swift
links.trackEvent("purchase", value: 49.99, currency: "USD", linkId: event.linkId) { ok in }
links.checkDeferred { event in }        // re-run the deferred check (debugging)
links.pendingOpenReports { count in }   // saved reports waiting to be sent
links.flushOpenReports { }              // send them now
```

The event carries the tap id of the most recent link open, as long as that open was in the last 7 days. The tap id comes from a browser hand-off to `yourapp://…?strait_click=…`, an open from a verified short link (Universal Link), or an install match. When our server matches an open or an install, it sends the tap id back with its answer. That lets Analytics put the revenue on the exact tap's channel and A/B variant. Each newer open replaces the remembered tap with its own, so an older tap never takes credit for a newer open; if an open comes with no tap id, the remembered one is forgotten and the event carries none. To name the tap yourself, pass `clickId:`, which overrides the remembered one. The server keeps it only if it's a tap of your workspace; otherwise it drops the id and still records the event.

The once-per-install flag and pending open reports live in `UserDefaults.standard` by default; pass any `StraitStorage` to change that. Callbacks run on the main queue.

When someone without your app taps a link in Safari, they see a page with a **Get the app** button. Tapping it saves a coarse, short-lived device match (screen width, pixel ratio, language, time zone, plus the network the request came from) and opens the App Store. On first launch the SDK sends the same fields; if they match within **1 hour**, your app gets the link. Nothing is read from the clipboard, so iOS shows no paste banner. Details in [Deferred deep linking](https://straitlink.in/docs/deferred-deep-linking/).

:::warn Check on a device before you ship
The library itself is tested in CI. The Unity glue below (MonoBehaviour, PlayerPrefs, AndroidJavaObject, the iOS plugin, UnityWebRequest) hasn't been run in the Unity editor or on a device yet. Treat it as a documented starting point.
:::

Requires Unity 2021.2+ with **Api Compatibility Level = .NET Standard 2.1**. In Unity: **Window → Package Manager → + → Add package from git URL…** and paste:

```text
https://github.com/bazingga08/strait-sdk-unity.git?path=src#v0.8.0
```

The package lives in the repo's `src/` folder, so keep the `?path=src` part. An OpenUPM listing is coming soon. Without Package Manager, copy the SDK's `src/*.cs` into your project (for example `Assets/Strait/`), or build the project and drop the DLL into `Assets/Plugins/`. Add `com.android.installreferrer:installreferrer:2.2` to your Android Gradle dependencies (custom `mainTemplate.gradle` or EDM4U).

The iPhone match compares what the browser saw at tap time with what the game reports, so the values must be the browser's: CSS screen width (portrait, rounded like Chrome) via `StraitCore.PortraitScreenWidth(w, h)` (the shorter side, so a game first opened in landscape still matches), device pixel ratio, locale and IANA time zone. Don't use `Screen.width`, which follows Unity's render scaling. The SDK README has full `StraitDevice.Collect` (Android via `AndroidJavaObject`, iOS via a tiny `.mm` plugin), `PlayReferrer.Get` and `UnityWebRequestTransport` implementations.

```csharp
await LinksBehaviour.Client.TrackEvent("purchase", value: 4.99, currency: "USD", linkId: lastLink?.LinkId);
```

`TrackEvent` carries the tap id of the most recent link open, as long as that open was in the last 7 days. The tap id comes from a browser hand-off to `yourapp://…?strait_click=…`, a Google Play install, an open from a verified short link, or an iPhone install match. When our server matches an open or an install, it sends the tap id back with its answer. That lets Analytics put the revenue on the exact tap's channel and A/B variant. Each newer open replaces the remembered tap with its own, so an older tap never takes credit for a newer open; if an open comes with no tap id, the remembered one is forgotten and the event carries none. To name the tap yourself, pass `clickId:`, which overrides the remembered one. The server keeps it only if it's a tap of your workspace; otherwise it drops the id and still records the event.

`LinkEvent` has the same fields and values as the other SDKs: `Id, Kind, Route, AppState, Matched, Reason, RawUrl, Url, Path, Params, LinkId, Ms, At`. Call `Start` and `HandleUrl` from the main thread; events fire on Unity's main thread.

The SDK isn't on the npm registry yet, so install it from GitHub (npm builds it during install). It installs as `@strait/sdk-web`, so imports stay the same once it's on npm.

```bash
npm install github:bazingga08/strait-sdk-web#v0.5.2
```

Coarse device fields only: screen width, pixel ratio, two-letter language and time zone, posted to `/v1/match`. Our server adds the network it sees the request from and computes the match. The browser never sends an IP address, and the match code is never used to identify someone across apps or sites.

| Export | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `resolveDeferredLink(config, opts?)` | The one call you need on launch |
| `computeSignature(inputs)` | The shared match signature (advanced / testing) |
| `h32(s)` | The shared hash (advanced / testing) |
