
| Method | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `createLink(input)` | `POST /v1/links` |
| `listLinks()` | `GET /v1/links` |
| `updateLink(slug, fields)` | `PATCH /v1/links/:slug` |
| `deleteLink(slug)` | `DELETE /v1/links/:slug` |
| `sendEvent(input)` | `POST /v1/event` |

Full request and response details are in the [REST API reference](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/).

```txt
https://acme.strait.link/summer   →   https://shop.example.com/product/42
        └ link domain ┘ └slug┘        └──────── destination ────────┘
```

- **Slug**: letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 64 characters. A few words are reserved (`v1`, `healthz`, `debug`…). If a slug is already taken you get `409`.
- **Destination** (`longUrl`): must be `https://`. Your app receives its path and query (`/product/42`), so use the same paths your app routes on.

:::note No website?
The destination can be any `https://` URL on a domain you control, or your default web URL (Dashboard → Settings) with the path you want, such as `https://yourapp.com/product/42`. Only the path and query reach your app. Desktop visitors go to the full URL, and so do people without the app if you chose "always your website", so it's best if that page exists.
:::

| Who taps | What happens |
|---|---|
| Android, app installed, verified link | The phone opens your app directly. The SDK resolves the link and reports the open. |
| Android, from a browser page | Our server hands the link to your app with your custom scheme. If the app isn't installed, the phone goes to Google Play (link kept for after install) or your website, as set in Settings. |
| iPhone, app installed | iOS opens your app directly via Universal Links. |
| iPhone, app not installed | Safari shows a page with a **Get the app** button that opens the App Store. The tap saves a short-lived match so the first open lands on the right screen (beta). |
| In-app browsers (Instagram, TikTok, X…) | These block apps and stores, so we show a page that helps the person open the link in their real browser. |
| Desktop | Redirects to the link's desktop URL, or the destination. |
| Link-preview robots (WhatsApp, Slack, iMessage…) | Get a preview page with the link's title, description and image. They're never redirected and never counted as taps. |

Every tap reaches Cloudflare first. What happens next depends on what the tap needs:

- **Plain redirects** are decided at the Cloudflare location nearest the person, without a round trip to our servers. This covers desktop taps, Android browser taps (to your app, Google Play or your website) and iPhone taps that go straight to the website or the App Store. The decision is made by the same code our server runs, so the person lands in the same place either way.
- **Everything else is served by our server**: pages (the iPhone **Get the app** page, in-app browser pages, password and expired pages), link-preview robots, and links with A/B destinations. A link close to its expiry time also goes to our server, so expiry is exact.

Both paths record the tap the same way: the same Analytics row, the same billing rules and the same `link.clicked` webhook. For a tap decided at the edge, the webhook is sent when our server receives the tap's record, a moment after the redirect. If that record can't be delivered straight away, it's kept and sent again later.

When you change or deactivate a link, or change your workspace settings, taps follow the new version within 30 seconds. Changes made through the API take effect straight away on our server and at the Cloudflare location that carried the request; other locations, and changes made in the dashboard, can take up to 30 seconds.

Each link can also have:

- **Per-platform fallbacks**: `iosFallbackUrl`, `androidFallbackUrl`, `desktopUrl` (all https).
- **Social preview**: title, description and image for chat-app previews.
- **Campaign, tags, folders and UTM parameters** to organise links and analytics.
- **Expiry**: after it, the link stops opening its destination. You choose where taps go instead (see below).
- **Password**: people must enter it before being redirected. Previews still work.
- **A/B destinations**: split taps across several destinations. Analytics shows which variant each tap got.
- **QR code**: download one for any link from the dashboard.

After its expiry time a link no longer opens its destination. You decide where people go instead. Set the default for every link in **Settings → When a link expires**, and change it for one link in its edit panel (or with the API fields below). A link with no setting of its own follows the workspace default.

| Option | What people see |
|---|---|
| **Show an 'expired' page** (default) | A short "This link has expired" page with your app's name and a link to your website. HTTP 410. |
| **Send to the app store** | Google Play on Android, the App Store on iPhone, using your app configuration. On Android the install referrer carries the tap, the same as any store hand-off. Computers, and phones whose store isn't set up, go to your expired-link web page if you set one, otherwise they see the expired page. |
| **Send to a web page** | Everyone goes to the https page you choose. If it's missing, or fails our phishing and malware check, people see the expired page instead. |

The store and web page options answer with a plain redirect (HTTP 302). Whichever option you pick, a tap on an expired link is recorded with **Sent to: expired**, plus where it went, and is never billed or sent as a `link.clicked` webhook. The dashboard Playground and `GET /v1/simulate` show the same decision as a real tap.

With the API, `POST /v1/links` and `PATCH /v1/links/{slug}` accept:

- `expiresAt`: epoch milliseconds or an ISO 8601 date-time (`null` in a PATCH removes the expiry).
- `expiredAction`: `page`, `store` or `url` (`null` in a PATCH goes back to the workspace default).
- `expiredUrl`: an https page. Required with `url`. With `store`, it's where computers go.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://strait.link/v1/links/summer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STRAIT_SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"expiredAction":"url","expiredUrl":"https://yourco.com/offers"}'
```
Deactivating a link (dashboard, or `DELETE /v1/links/{slug}`) stops it resolving. Visitors see a not-found page that links to your website if one is set in Settings.
Links used for phishing, malware or spam are disabled under the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://straitlink.in/legal/acceptable-use/). A disabled link shows a warning page instead of redirecting.

Android App Links and iPhone Universal Links are verified **per domain**. The phone downloads a small file from the link's domain that says which app may open its links:

- `https://acme.strait.link/.well-known/assetlinks.json` (Android)
- `https://acme.strait.link/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` (iPhone)

If every customer shared one domain, that file could only name one app, and everyone else's links would open the browser. So each workspace gets its own subdomain, and we serve your app's files from it, built from the details in **Dashboard → Settings**.

A slug is unique within your workspace, not across Strait. Two workspaces can both have `/summer`: `https://acme.strait.link/summer` and `https://globex.strait.link/summer` are different links that open different apps.

That's why you should **always share your handle URL**, never the bare `https://strait.link/summer`. The bare `strait.link` root only answers a slug that no other workspace uses, so links shared before workspaces had their own domains keep working. Once a second workspace creates the same slug, the bare address finds nothing. The API returns the right address for every link as `shortUrl`, and the dashboard copies it for you.

Your handle comes from your workspace name when you sign up (for example "Acme Inc." becomes `acme-inc`). Handles are 3 to 30 characters: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Some words, like `www`, `api` and `status`, are reserved for our own use.

:::warn Choose your handle before your first link
The workspace owner can rename the handle in **Dashboard → Get started** (or **Settings**) until the workspace creates its first link. After that it's fixed, because links you've shared and the App Links / Universal Links setup in your app depend on it.
:::

Use your link domain in three places:

1. **The SDK `endpoint`**: `https://acme.strait.link`
2. **Android**: the `android:host` of your App Links intent filter
3. **iPhone**: the Associated Domains entry `applinks:acme.strait.link`

Custom domains: coming soon. Today every workspace gets `<handle>.strait.link`, with HTTPS, on every plan. Serving links on your own domain (such as `links.yourcompany.com`) needs automatic certificates and domain verification, which we haven't built yet. We'll update this page when it's ready.

:::note
After changing your app's signing keys or team ID, phones and Google's verifier re-read the files on their own schedule. We serve them with a short cache (10 minutes), but Android can take longer to re-verify an installed app. Reinstalling the app forces a fresh check.
:::

From the app details in **Dashboard → Settings**, your link domain serves:

| File | Built from | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` | Package name + every SHA-256 fingerprint you list | Android, to verify App Links |
| `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` | Apple Team ID + bundle ID | iPhone, to verify Universal Links |

Each file returns `404` until the matching fields are filled in. Check yours:

```bash
curl https://acme.strait.link/.well-known/assetlinks.json
curl https://acme.strait.link/.well-known/apple-app-site-association
```

Or paste your link domain into the [App Links checker](https://straitlink.in/tools/app-links-checker/), which checks both files and explains any problem.

1. Add an intent filter with `android:autoVerify="true"` for `https://acme.strait.link` ([example](https://straitlink.in/docs/quick-start/#5-let-the-phone-open-your-app)).
2. List **every** certificate fingerprint your app is signed with in Settings: debug, upload, and the Play App Signing key from Play Console. A Play-installed app is signed by Google's key, not yours. Fingerprints are checked when you save: each one is stored as 32 uppercase hex pairs joined by colons (`FA:C6:17:…`), duplicates are dropped, and anything that isn't a SHA-256 fingerprint is refused. The package name must look like a Java package (`com.yourco.app`), and the website fallback must be `https://`.
3. Install the app. Android checks the file at install time.

Check verification on a connected phone:

```bash
adb shell pm get-app-links com.yourco.app
# Look for:  acme.strait.link: verified
```

If it says `1024` or `none`, Android couldn't verify. See [Troubleshooting](https://straitlink.in/docs/troubleshooting/#the-link-opens-the-browser-instead-of-the-app).

1. Add the **Associated Domains** capability with `applinks:acme.strait.link`.
2. Save your Apple Team ID and bundle ID in Settings.
3. Install the app. iOS fetches the file through Apple's CDN, which can lag behind changes.

When a tap can't open your app straight away, the person sees one of our pages: the iPhone "Get the app" page, the page inside an in-app browser (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp…) with **Open in app**, the password page, and the "not found" and "This link has expired" pages. They lead with your app, not with Strait. Set these optional fields in **Dashboard → Settings → How your link pages look**:

| Field | Rules | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| App name | 1 to 60 characters, no line breaks | "Opens Acme Shop…", "Go to Acme Shop's website" |
| Icon URL | `https://` only (people's phones load it). Square works best | The icon at the top of each page |
| Brand colour | A hex colour such as `#7c3aed` (`#abc` is fine too) | The main button. We pick black or white text on it so it stays readable (contrast at least 4.5:1) |

Invalid values are refused when you save, with a message saying why. Leave them empty and the pages use neutral defaults. Every page works in light and dark mode. The page we show for a link we've disabled for safety stays unbranded on purpose. See the [home page](https://straitlink.in/#what-users-see) for real screenshots.

When a tap reaches our server in a browser (for example from a web page, or on Android when the link isn't verified), we hand the link to your app using your custom scheme:

```txt
yourapp://shop.example.com/product/42?strait_click=<tap id>
```

The SDK turns that into the destination `https://shop.example.com/product/42`, removes the tap id before your app sees it, and uses the id to join the app open to the exact tap in Analytics.

When someone without your app taps a link on Android, we send them to Google Play with the link attached to the install:

```txt
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.yourco.app&referrer=strait_link%3D<link id>%26strait_click%3D<tap id>
```

Google Play keeps that referrer through the install. On first open, the SDK reads it, asks our server for the link (`/v1/referrer`), and routes your app there. It's **deterministic**: no guessing, and the install is joined to the exact tap.

To test it you need a build installed **from Google Play**. An internal testing track works. Sideloaded builds have no referrer.

If there's no referrer link (the app was found in a store search, for example), the SDK still checks in once so the install is counted in your match rate. Don't expect a match in that case on Android.

iOS doesn't pass anything through the App Store, and reading the clipboard triggers a "pasted from Safari" banner. We don't use the clipboard. Instead:

1. Someone without your app taps the link in Safari and sees a page with a **Get the app** button.
2. Tapping it records a coarse device signature together with the link, then opens the App Store.
3. On first launch, the SDK sends the same coarse fields to `/v1/match`. If a signature from the last **1 hour** matches, your app gets the link.

The signature is made from:

| Input | From |
|---|---|
| Screen width and pixel ratio | The browser, then the app |
| Language and time zone | The browser, then the app |
| iOS major version | The browser's user agent, then the app's |
| Network: prefix, operator (ASN) and a keyed hash of the full IP | Seen by our server; never sent by the app |

Each saved signature can be matched **once** and expires after one hour. It's never used to identify anyone across apps or sites.

:::warn Probabilistic, and in beta
Two people on the same network with the same phone model, language and time zone who tap different links within the hour are **not matched at all**: when taps look alike, we refuse rather than guess, so neither install is sent to the wrong screen. Each match in Analytics shows its method, so you can see how installs were matched. iPhone matching hasn't been proven on a real device yet.
:::

Either way, a matched install comes back to the app with its tap id, so purchases made afterwards are credited to that tap (see [Purchases](https://straitlink.in/docs/analytics/#purchases)).

Every install in Analytics shows how it was matched:

| Method | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `install_referrer` | Exact, from the Google Play referrer |
| `exact_ext` | iPhone signature matched on every input |
| `exact_core` | iPhone signature matched on the core inputs |
| `none` | No match: organic install, or the match window passed |

The deferred check runs once per install. It's skipped (and marked done) when the first launch was itself opened by a link, so a direct open is never followed by a stale deferred jump. If the phone is offline on first launch, the check runs again next launch.

```txt
Taps  →  Where we sent them  →  App opened  →  Installs  →  Purchases
```

Each step is joined to the step before it with a tap id, so you can follow one tap all the way to revenue.

**Taps** are each time someone tapped one of your links.

- Taps that go through our server in a browser are counted when they arrive.
- A verified link can open your app directly from WhatsApp, Gmail and so on without touching our server. Those are counted when your app reports the open through the SDK.
- If a browser loads the link and then hands it to your app (Edge does this), it's still one tap.
- Link-preview robots are never counted.

**Where we sent them** is decided per device: app or store, app or website, store, website, the iPhone "Get the app" page, or the in-app-browser page. On Android the phone then makes the final choice: your app if installed, otherwise the store or website.

- **Opened the app**: browser taps where your app then opened and reported that exact tap, plus verified-link opens.
- **Open rate**: taps that opened the app (directly or via the browser), divided by all taps.
- **New users**: the first launch after installing the app. **Existing users**: already had it installed.
- **App state** at open: *closed* (the link launched the app), *background* (it brought the app back), *foreground* (the app was already on screen).
- **Unresolved opens**: a link opened the app but couldn't be resolved (expired, deleted, wrong workspace), so the person didn't land on the right screen.

Opens are reported once each. If the phone is offline, the SDK saves the report and sends it later (up to 7 days), and duplicates are ignored.

- **Installs from links**: first launches of a new install that we tied to one of your links.
- **Joined to the exact tap**: of those, the ones matched to the precise tap (Play install referrer or browser hand-off), not just the link.
- **Unattributed installs**: first launches no link could be found for: store search, word of mouth, or a match that failed.
- **Match rate**: installs reconnected to a tap, divided by all attributable installs.
- **Time to install**: the median time between tap and install, for installs matched to their tap.
- **Probably reached the store / website**: store-bound browser taps where the app never opened and no install followed. We can't see the store page itself, so these are estimates and labelled as such.

Send events from your app (`trackEvent`) or server (`POST /v1/event`) with an optional value, currency and link id. They appear as the last step of the funnel, with revenue.

Events can also carry `clickId`, the tap they came from, so revenue lands on that tap's channel and A/B variant. The app SDKs fill it in for you from the most recent link open within 7 days. The tap id reaches the app four ways: in a browser hand-off, in the Google Play install referrer, and in our server's answer when it matches an open from a verified short link or an iPhone install. Each newer open replaces the remembered tap with its own. An explicit `clickId` overrides it. A `clickId` that isn't a tap of your workspace is dropped, and the event is still recorded.

**An install that is never opened.** Until your app launches, no linking product can see it. Only Google Play Console and App Store Connect report raw installs. Expect our install numbers to be lower than the stores' for that reason.

Taps keep the network prefix (first three parts of the IP address, never the full address), platform, device class and OS version. App opens store the host and path of the URL, never the query string. See the [Privacy Policy](https://straitlink.in/legal/privacy/).

```txt
https://strait.link
```

The machine-readable description is at `https://strait.link/v1/openapi.json`. Import it into Postman, Insomnia or a code generator.

| Key | Send it as | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| Secret key `st_live_…` | `Authorization: Bearer st_live_…` header | Link endpoints, and events from your server |
| Publishable key `st_pub_live_…` | `"publishableKey"` in the JSON body | Endpoints your app or website calls |

The publishable key is in **Dashboard → Get started** and secret keys are in **Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys**. The examples on this page read the secret key from an environment variable:

```bash
export SECRET_KEY=st_live_…   # Dashboard → Settings → Secret keys
```

 The publishable key is safe to ship in apps; it can only resolve links, report opens, match installs and send events. Requests with a missing or wrong key get `401`.

After you rotate the publishable key, the old key keeps working for 7 days so apps already on people's phones don't break. Responses to the old key carry a `Strait-Key-Deprecated` header with the time it stops working (ISO 8601, for example `Strait-Key-Deprecated: 2026-01-08T12:00:00.000Z`); after that it gets `401`. See [Keys](https://straitlink.in/docs/#rotating-keys).

Every error under `/v1` is JSON with an `error` message, never an HTML page:

```json
{ "error": "slug already exists in this workspace" }
```

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `400` | Invalid input, including a body that isn't valid JSON (`{ "error": "malformed JSON body" }`) |
| `401` | Missing or wrong key |
| `402` | Plan limit reached when creating a link. Adds `reason` (`links`, or `clicks` for the monthly tap limit) and `upgradeUrl`; existing links keep working |
| `404` | Not found, including unknown `/v1` paths (`{ "error": "not found" }`) |
| `409` | The slug is already used by an active link in your workspace |
| `413` | Request body too large |
| `429` | Rate limited |
| `500` | Our fault: `{ "error": "internal error" }`, with no internal details |

Some errors add fields, for example a blocked destination returns `{ "error": "destination_blocked", "reason": "…" }`. The endpoints apps call are rate-limited per IP address; normal SDK traffic is far below the limit.

Slugs are unique within your workspace, not across Strait: another workspace can also have `/summer` on its own link domain. Every link the API returns includes `shortUrl`, the address to share: `https://<your-handle>.strait.link/<slug>`. Always share `shortUrl`. See [Link domains](https://straitlink.in/docs/link-domains/).

Fetch one link by its slug with `GET /v1/links/{slug}`.

Link edits (`PATCH /v1/links/{slug}`) and deactivations (`DELETE /v1/links/{slug}`) apply to taps within 30 seconds. They apply straight away on our server and at the Cloudflare location that carried your request; plain redirects decided at other Cloudflare locations can follow the old version for up to 30 seconds. See [How a tap is handled](https://straitlink.in/docs/short-links/#how-a-tap-is-handled).

`GET /v1/links` without parameters returns every active link as a plain JSON array. Add `limit` (1 to 100, default 50) or `cursor` to page through them instead, newest first:

```bash
curl "https://strait.link/v1/links?limit=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
# → { "links": [ … ], "nextCursor": "WyIyMDI2…" }

curl "https://strait.link/v1/links?limit=50&cursor=WyIyMDI2…" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
# → { "links": [ … ], "nextCursor": null }   ← the last page
```

Pass each `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is `null`. Treat the cursor as opaque; an invalid one gets `400`.

sections.section: Try a link without tapping it
sections.markdown:
`GET /v1/simulate` tells you what a tap would do, without recording a tap, sending webhooks or counting toward your plan. Pass the full short link as `url` and either a raw user agent or one of these presets as `ua`: `android`, `iphone`, `ipad`, `desktop`, `instagram-ios`, `instagram-android`, `facebook-android`, `whatsapp-android`, `bot`.

```bash
curl "https://strait.link/v1/simulate?url=https%3A%2F%2Facme.strait.link%2Fsummer&ua=instagram-android" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
```

The answer has the `decision` (`redirect`, `interstitial`, `escape`, `preview`, `expired` or `blocked`), `sentTo` (the same values as Analytics, below), the `location` the visitor would be sent to (or the main button's target on a page), and a plain-English `reason`. Hand-off URLs in it carry a placeholder tap id, `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000`. You can also authenticate with `publishableKey=` as a query parameter; the link must belong to the key's workspace. **Dashboard → Playground** runs the same check.

Each tap is recorded with where we sent it, `sent_to` (in the taps export and the `sentTo` webhook field):

| `sent_to` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `app_or_store` | Android: your app if installed, otherwise the store |
| `app_or_website` | Android: your app if installed, otherwise your website |
| `store` | Straight to Google Play or the App Store |
| `website` | Straight to the destination or fallback website |
| `app_store_page` | The iPhone "Get the app" page |
| `in_app_browser_page` | The page shown inside an in-app browser (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp…) with "Open in app" |
| `expired` | The link had expired: the visitor saw "This link has expired". Recorded, never billed, no webhook |

Taps decided at Cloudflare's edge and taps served by our server are recorded with the same fields and labels.

A tap's **channel** is the first of these that has a value: the tap URL's `utm_source`, the link destination's `utm_source`, the in-app browser it was tapped in (`whatsapp`, `instagram`…), then the referring site. Taps with none of these are direct.

A link's **campaign** is the `campaign` you set. If you leave it out, it's filled in from the destination's `utm_campaign`, and follows it when you change the destination.

`POST /v1/links` also accepts these optional fields (all URLs must be https):

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `iosFallbackUrl`, `androidFallbackUrl`, `desktopUrl` | Where to send people on that platform when the app can't open |
| `title`, `description`, `imageUrl` | The preview shown in chat apps and social posts |
| `campaign` | Campaign name for analytics (also passed to the App Store as the campaign token). Defaults to the destination's `utm_campaign` |
| `tags` | Labels for filtering |
| `expiresAt` | When the link expires: epoch milliseconds or an ISO 8601 date-time |
| `expiredAction`, `expiredUrl` | Where taps go after expiry: `page`, `store` or `url` (with an https `expiredUrl`). Leave out to use the workspace setting. See [When a link expires](https://straitlink.in/docs/short-links/#when-a-link-expires) |

`PATCH /v1/links/{slug}` changes `longUrl`, `title`, `tags`, `expiresAt`, `expiredAction` and `expiredUrl`. Send only what changes; `null` clears `expiresAt` (never expires) and `expiredAction` (back to the workspace setting).

`POST /v1/links/batch` creates up to 500 links in one call, for imports and migrations. Send `{ "links": [ … ] }`, where each item takes the same fields as `POST /v1/links`. Every item is checked the same way (slug rules, https destinations, the unsafe-destination check, plan limits) and gets its own result, so one bad item never fails the batch:

```bash
curl https://strait.link/v1/links/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "links": [ { "slug": "spring", "longUrl": "https://shop.example.com/spring" },
                  { "slug": "summer", "longUrl": "https://shop.example.com/summer", "campaign": "summer_2026" } ] }'
# → { "results": [ { "index": 0, "ok": true, "status": 201, "link": { … } }, … ],
#     "summary": { "total": 2, "created": 2, "failed": 0 } }
```

The response is `200` whenever the request itself is valid; read each item's `ok` and `status` (`201`, `400`, `402` or `409`). A slug that already exists, or repeats earlier in the same batch, is a `409` for that item only, so re-running an import is safe. Items past a plan limit get `402`. See [Migrate from Branch](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-branch/).

Export everything in your workspace at any time, on every plan. It gives you what you need to leave, or to keep your links running if Strait ever shuts down. Send your secret key; a publishable key gets `401`.

```txt
GET https://strait.link/v1/export?part=links|taps|events|webhooks|worker
Authorization: Bearer st_live_…
```

| `part` | What you get |
|---|---|
| `links` | NDJSON, one link per line: slug, destination, platform fallbacks and whether it is active |
| `taps` | CSV of every tap, joined to the app opens and installs that came from it. No date cap; add optional `from` and `to` (ISO dates) to narrow it |
| `events` | CSV of every conversion event (signups, purchases, revenue): `created_at, name, value, currency, platform, link_id, slug, click_id, channel, campaign, variant`. `channel`, `campaign` and `variant` come from the tap the event is attributed to, when it has a `click_id`. Oldest first, no date cap; optional `from` and `to` |
| `webhooks` | JSON of your webhook settings: `url`, `events`, `active` and `createdAt` for each one. Signing secrets are never exported; make new ones when you recreate a webhook |
| `worker` | A single-file Cloudflare Worker that keeps your links redirecting, with the Android, iPhone and desktop fallbacks built in. Deploy it on your own account |

```bash
curl "https://strait.link/v1/export?part=events&from=2026-01-01" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY" -o events.csv
```

Taps and events are streamed page by page, so an export of millions of rows starts straight away and never times out on our side.

### Download from the dashboard

Owners and admins can download every part from **Dashboard → Settings → Download everything**: one button per file, no secret key needed. Members and viewers can't, because an export contains all of the workspace's data. The same section keeps the commands above under **Or from your server**.

Each button asks for a one-time download link, then your browser saves the file directly, however large:

```txt
POST https://strait.link/v1/export/token      {"part": "events"}
→ 201 {"token": "stx_…", "expiresAt": "…", "path": "/v1/export?part=events&token=stx_…"}
GET  https://strait.link/v1/export?part=events&token=stx_…
```

The token works once, for 60 seconds, for that part (and its `from` / `to`) only. Only a hash of it is stored. A used or expired token gets `401`.
The SDKs call the publishable-key endpoints below for you; you only need them if you're writing your own client.

In **Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks**, add an `https://` URL and pick events. You'll see the **signing secret** once; store it on your server. Free includes 1 webhook, Starter 3 and Scale 10 ([pricing](https://straitlink.in/pricing/)).

The URL must be a public `https://` address. When you save it, we refuse:

- `http://` and other schemes, and URLs with a username or password in them
- `localhost`, and hosts ending in `.localhost`, `.local` or `.internal`
- IP addresses in private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade NAT (100.64.0.0/10), multicast and reserved ranges, IPv4 and IPv6

We check again before every delivery, after looking up the hostname, because DNS can change after you save. A URL that now points at a private address isn't sent to and isn't retried.

Press **Send test event** next to a webhook in **Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks**. We send one `ping` event to it straight away, signed like every other delivery, and show what your server answered: the status code, the first 500 characters of the response body and how long it took. It works on a paused webhook too. Test events aren't stored or retried.

From your server, call the same thing with your secret key:

```bash
curl -X POST https://strait.link/v1/webhooks/<webhook id>/test \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET_KEY"
```

```json title="Response"
{
  "delivered": true,
  "status": 204,
  "error": null,
  "body": "",
  "durationMs": 182,
  "deliveryId": "0b9c3f0e-5a7d-4a51-9a2e-3f1c8d2b6e47",
  "event": "ping"
}
```

When the delivery fails, `delivered` is `false` and `error` says why: `HTTP 500` (your server's status), `timeout` (no answer within 5 seconds) or `unsafe_target` (the URL resolves to a private address). An unknown webhook id, or one from another workspace, gets `404`.

| Event | Sent when | `data` fields |
|---|---|---|
| `link.clicked` | Someone taps a link (browser taps, and verified-link opens your app reports) | `linkId`, `slug`, `platform`, `clickId`, `sentTo`, `deviceClass`, `variant`, `source` |
| `install.matched` | A first launch after install is matched to a link | `linkId`, `clickId`, `matchMethod`, `platform` |
| `app.opened` | A link opens your app | `linkId`, `clickId`, `kind`, `route`, `appState`, `isInstall`, `matched`, `platform` |
| `ping` | You send a test event | `webhookId`, `message` |

Fields that don't apply to an event are left out. Taps on an expired link are recorded in Analytics but don't send `link.clicked`.

```http title="Request we send"
POST /your/webhook HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
X-Strait-Event: install.matched
X-Strait-Delivery: 7f3e2c1a-9b4d-4e8f-a6c5-2d1b0e9f8a73
X-Strait-Attempt: 1
X-Strait-Signature: t=1767225600,v1=6a1f0c3e9b…

{
  "id": "7f3e2c1a-9b4d-4e8f-a6c5-2d1b0e9f8a73",
  "event": "install.matched",
  "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "data": {
    "linkId": "lnk_123",
    "clickId": "c_123",
    "matchMethod": "install_referrer",
    "platform": "android"
  }
}
```

- Each request times out after 5 seconds. Respond quickly with any `2xx` and do the work afterwards.
- Redirects aren't followed: a `3xx` counts as a failed attempt.
- **Retries:** anything other than a `2xx` (or no answer) is retried after 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 1 hour and 6 hours, six attempts in total, then marked failed. Your server can be down for hours without losing events.
- Each event has a stable id: `X-Strait-Delivery` (the same as `id` in the body) stays the same on every retry, and `X-Strait-Attempt` counts up. Store the ids you've handled and ignore repeats: delivery is **at least once**.
- Every attempt is signed again with a fresh timestamp, so a retry six hours later still passes the 5-minute check.
- Addresses that resolve to private networks are never sent to or retried.

Open **Deliveries** under a webhook in **Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks** to see its last 20 deliveries: the event, when it was created, its status (**Delivered**, **Retrying** or **Failed** after all six attempts), how many attempts it took and your server's last answer. A failed delivery, or one waiting for its next retry, has a **Redeliver** button: fix your endpoint (or change the webhook URL), press it, and we send the same event again right away. Owners, admins and members can redeliver; viewers can only look.

The same from your server, with a secret key:

```txt
GET https://strait.link/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries?limit=20&cursor=…
Authorization: Bearer st_live_…
```

```json
{
  "deliveries": [
    {
      "id": "7f3e2c1a-9b4d-4e8f-a6c5-2d1b0e9f8a73",
      "webhookId": "5d0c…",
      "event": "link.clicked",
      "status": "failed",
      "attempts": 6,
      "lastStatus": 500,
      "lastError": "HTTP 500",
      "nextAttemptAt": null,
      "createdAt": "2026-10-04T09:12:03.512Z",
      "deliveredAt": null
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": null
}
```

Newest first, `limit` 1 to 100 (default 20); pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next page. Payloads aren't returned. `nextAttemptAt` is set while a delivery is waiting for a retry.

```txt
POST https://strait.link/v1/webhook-deliveries/{id}/redeliver
Authorization: Bearer st_live_…
```

This queues the delivery again with its attempt count reset, sends it at once to the webhook's **current** URL with the same `X-Strait-Delivery` id, and answers with the delivery after that attempt (same shape as above). If it fails again it gets the full retry schedule. You get `409` when it was already delivered, or while it's being sent (in its first 2 minutes, or claimed by a delivery worker right now): try again shortly. A delivery from another workspace is `404`.

Delivery history is kept for 30 days, then deleted by a nightly job.

| Firebase Dynamic Links | Strait |
|---|---|
| `yourapp.page.link` domain | Your workspace link domain, `<handle>.strait.link`. Custom domains are coming soon |
| Dynamic Link `link=` parameter (deep link) | The link's destination (`longUrl`) |
| Android / iOS fallback parameters (`afl`, `ifl`) | `androidFallbackUrl`, `iosFallbackUrl` |
| Social meta tags (`st`, `sd`, `si`) | `title`, `description`, `imageUrl` |
| Campaign parameters (`utm_*`) | UTM parameters and `campaign` |
| `FirebaseDynamicLinks.getDynamicLink()` / pending link on first open | The SDK's `onLink` callback (direct and deferred) |
| Firebase Analytics link events | Built-in Analytics: taps, opens, installs, purchases |

Collect your links in any of these forms, one per line:

- Firebase short links with the long form attached, like `https://yourapp.page.link/abc?link=https%3A%2F%2Fshop.example.com%2Fp%2F42`
- Plain destination URLs
- A CSV with a header row. We recognise `link`, `url`, `destination` or `longUrl` for the destination, and `slug`, `short`, `path` or `key` for the slug.

```txt title="links.csv"
short,link
https://yourapp.page.link/summer,https://shop.example.com/product/42
https://yourapp.page.link/invite,https://shop.example.com/invite?ref=abc
```

In **Dashboard → Import**, paste the list. We pull the real destination out of each Firebase link's `link=` parameter, keep the old short code as the slug where we can, and show a preview with any rows that can't be imported (and why) before you confirm.

Replace your `page.link` domain with your link domain:

- **Android**: change the intent filter's `android:host` to `acme.strait.link`, and add your SHA-256 fingerprints in Settings.
- **iPhone**: change Associated Domains to `applinks:acme.strait.link`, and add your Team ID and bundle ID in Settings.

Wherever your backend called the Firebase REST API to shorten links, call `POST /v1/links` with your secret key, or use the [Node SDK](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/node/).

Coming from Branch instead? See [Migrate from Branch](https://straitlink.in/docs/migrate-from-branch/).

`page.link` domains belong to Google. Old links printed or posted on that domain can't be redirected by anyone else, so replace them wherever you still control the text (your website, emails, app screens). Links you create on Strait live on your own workspace subdomain, `<handle>.strait.link`, and you can [export them](https://straitlink.in/docs/api/#export) at any time. Custom domains are coming soon.

| Branch | Strait |
|---|---|
| `yourapp.app.link` domain (or your Branch custom domain) | Your workspace link domain, `<handle>.strait.link`. Custom domains are coming soon |
| Link alias / short path | The link's slug |
| `$deeplink_path` (what the app routes on) | The path and query of the link's destination (`longUrl`). The SDK hands your app `e.path` and `e.params` |
| `$canonical_url`, `$fallback_url`, `$desktop_url` | `longUrl` / `desktopUrl` |
| `$ios_url`, `$android_url` | `iosFallbackUrl`, `androidFallbackUrl` |
| `$og_title`, `$og_description`, `$og_image_url` | `title`, `description`, `imageUrl` |
| `~campaign` | `campaign` |
| `~channel` | `utm_source` on the destination (that's where Strait reads a link's channel from) |
| `~tags`, `~feature` | `tags` (the feature becomes a `feature:<name>` tag) |
| `Branch.getAutoInstance()` / `initSession` callback | The SDK's `onLink` callback (direct and deferred) |
| `BranchEvent` / custom events | `trackEvent` |

Download your links from your Branch dashboard's link export, as CSV or JSON. The first row of a CSV must be the header row with Branch's field names (`url`, `alias`, `$canonical_url`, `$deeplink_path`, `~campaign` and so on). JSON can be a list of links, `{ "links": [ … ] }`, or one link per line, and link data can sit at the top level or under `data` the way Branch's API returns it.

```txt title="branch-links.csv (shortened)"
url,$canonical_url,$deeplink_path,$ios_url,$android_url,$og_title,~campaign,~channel,~tags
https://acme.app.link/summer-sale,https://shop.example.com/sale/summer,,,,Summer Sale,summer_2026,instagram,"sale,summer"
https://acme.app.link/p42,https://shop.example.com/products/42,product/42,https://shop.example.com/ios/42,https://shop.example.com/android/42,,,,
```

**Slug.** The link's `alias` if it has one, else the last part of the Branch short link (`https://acme.app.link/summer-sale` becomes `summer-sale`), else the Branch link id (`~id`). Slugs can contain letters, numbers, `-` and `_` (up to 64), so other characters become `-`: `Invite%20Friend` becomes `Invite-Friend`. If that makes two different Branch links land on the same slug, the second gets `-2`. A slug that appears twice in the file, or that a live link in your workspace already uses, is shown as a problem and not imported.

**Destination and deep link path.** Strait routes your app by the destination's path and query: a tap on a link whose `longUrl` is `https://shop.example.com/product/42?ref=x` gives your app `e.path = "/product/42"` and `e.params = { ref: "x" }`. So:

- **No `$deeplink_path`:** `longUrl` is `$canonical_url`, else `$fallback_url`, else `$desktop_url`.
- **With a `$deeplink_path`:** `longUrl` is the web URL's origin plus the deep link path. With `$canonical_url = https://shop.example.com/products/42` and `$deeplink_path = product/42`, `longUrl` is `https://shop.example.com/product/42`, and the app gets `/product/42`. A custom-scheme path loses its scheme: `myapp://invite?code=XYZ` becomes `/invite?code=XYZ`. If a link has a deep link path but no web URL at all, enter your website in the import screen and it is used as the origin.
- **Different `$ios_deeplink_path` and `$android_deeplink_path`:** Strait has one in-app path for both platforms, so the Android path is used and the row shows a warning. Make sure both apps handle it.

Because the deep link path may not be a real page on your website, the original web page is kept for people without the app: `desktopUrl` becomes the canonical/fallback URL (unless `$desktop_url` is set), and so do `iosFallbackUrl` and `androidFallbackUrl` (unless `$ios_url` / `$android_url` are set).

**Platform fallbacks.** `$ios_url` → `iosFallbackUrl` and `$android_url` → `androidFallbackUrl`: where someone without the app goes on that platform when your workspace sends them to a website rather than the store.

**Social previews.** `$og_title` → `title` (or `$marketing_title` when there's no `$og_title`), `$og_description` → `description`, `$og_image_url` → `imageUrl`.

**Campaigns.** `~campaign` → `campaign`. `~channel` is added to the destination as `utm_source` (unless it already has one), which is how Strait labels a link's channel in [Analytics](https://straitlink.in/docs/analytics/). `~tags` become tags, and `~feature` adds a `feature:<name>` tag.

**Everything must be https.** A destination that isn't `https://` stops the row; an optional URL that isn't (for example an `http://` preview image) is left out and the row shows a warning.

**Other fields are not imported.** The preview lists every field in your file that Strait doesn't use, such as `~stage`, `~creation_source`, `$one_time_use` and your own custom link data keys. If your app reads custom link data, put what it needs into the deep link path or its query string before you import.

1. **Import and test.** Import your links, then tap a few on a real phone with the app installed and without it, and on a desktop browser.
2. **Ship the app update** with the Strait SDK and the new verification domain. You can keep the Branch SDK in the same release so old Branch links still open the app for people on it.
3. **Create new links on Strait.** Point your backend, marketing tools and share buttons at `POST /v1/links` (or the [Node SDK](https://straitlink.in/docs/sdks/node/)). New links live on `<handle>.strait.link`.
4. **Keep Branch active while old links circulate.** Links on `app.link` are served by Branch, and only while your Branch account is active. Replace them wherever you still control the text (website, emails, app screens, QR codes you can reprint), then let the rest age out before you close the Branch account.
5. **Remove the Branch SDK** in a later app release, once taps on old links have dropped off.

If you used a custom domain with Branch, it can't move to Strait yet: custom domains are coming soon. Until then, new links use `<handle>.strait.link`.

- **Analytics history.** Branch's clicks, installs, opens and attribution data stay in Branch. Export the reports you need before you close the account. Strait counts from the day your links and app switch over.
- **The `app.link` domain.** It belongs to Branch. Links on it keep working only while your Branch account is active, and nobody else can redirect them.
- **A Branch custom domain.** Not yet: custom domains are coming soon.
- **Custom link data** beyond the deep link path and query, and Branch settings such as `$one_time_use`, `$match_duration` or journeys and banners. The import lists every field it leaves out.
- **Separate iOS and Android deep link paths.** One path is kept for both.

sections.section: The link opens the browser instead of the app
sections.markdown:
This almost always means the phone couldn't verify that your app may open links on your domain.

Start with the free [App Links checker](https://straitlink.in/tools/app-links-checker/): it fetches both files from your domain and explains what's wrong with them (missing file, redirect, wrong content type, malformed fingerprint or app ID).

1. **Check the file.** `curl https://acme.strait.link/.well-known/assetlinks.json` should list your package name and fingerprints. A `404` means the Android fields in Settings are empty.
2. **Check the SHA-256.** The fingerprint must match the certificate of the build on the phone:
   - Debug builds: your debug keystore.
   - Release builds you install yourself: your upload key.
   - Builds from Google Play: the **App signing key** in Play Console → App integrity. This is Google's key, not yours.
3. **Check the intent filter**: `android:autoVerify="true"`, `https` scheme, and `android:host="acme.strait.link"` exactly.
4. **Re-verify.** Android checks at install time. Reinstall the app, then run `adb shell pm get-app-links com.yourco.app`. You want `verified`.
5. **Tap, don't type.** Pasting a link into the address bar never opens an app. Test from Messages, WhatsApp or Gmail.

On iPhone (beta): check `apple-app-site-association` lists `<Team ID>.<bundle ID>`, and the app has `applinks:acme.strait.link` in Associated Domains. iOS caches the file through Apple's CDN, so changes can take a while to show.

Samsung Internet handles our hand-off like Chrome: if the app is installed it opens; if not, it goes to Google Play. If Samsung Internet keeps opening links in the browser, check **Settings → Useful features → Open links in other apps** is on.

sections.section: Firefox and Edge ask before opening the app
sections.markdown: Firefox ("Open this link in …?") and Edge ("wants to open an external app") show a confirmation before handing a link to an app. That's the browser's choice and can't be skipped. Once the person confirms, the app opens on the right screen and the tap is counted once.

In-app browsers block apps and app stores, so a deep link can't work inside them. We detect them and show a page that helps the person open the link in their real browser, where it works normally. To skip that step, share links where possible as plain links that open outside the in-app browser, for example in WhatsApp, Messages or email.

sections.section: The deferred link didn't open the right screen after install
sections.markdown:
- **Android**: the app must be installed **from Google Play** (internal testing is fine). Sideloaded builds have no install referrer. In Settings, set "When someone without the app taps a link" to **Always Google Play** while your app isn't public, otherwise we send people to your website to avoid Play's "Item not found" page.
- **iPhone (beta)**: the person must tap **Get the app** on our page in Safari, and open the app within an hour, on the same network. A different network (Wi-Fi to cellular) will usually prevent a match.
- **Both**: the deferred check runs once per install. Uninstall and reinstall to test again.

sections.section: The app opened but `matched` is false
sections.markdown:
Check `reason` on the link event:

| Reason | What it means |
|---|---|
| `not_found` | No such link in this workspace (check the publishable key and the slug) |
| `expired` | The link's expiry has passed |
| `password_protected` | Password links can't be opened directly in the app |
| `no_match` | Deferred: no recent matching tap |
| `network` | The phone couldn't reach us. The open is saved and reported later |
| `invalid_url` | The URL couldn't be parsed |
Email [support@straitlink.in](mailto:support@straitlink.in) with the link, the phone model, the browser or app you tapped it in, and what happened.
